blocks.text: Setting up Excel for compliance audits

Compliance officers must ensure every entry is accurate. Start by using Data Validation to restrict what users can enter in your sheets. Go to Data > Data Validation to create drop down lists for things like employee status or department names. This prevents typos that break your pivot tables later. If you need to track dates, use the shortcut ⌃ ; to insert the current date instantly. This keeps your records timestamped without manual entry errors.
Managing large HR datasets on a Mac

Excel on Mac handles up to 1,048,576 rows. Large files can get sluggish if you have too many formulas. Use the Paste Special feature to replace formulas with static values once you finish a calculation. Copy your range, press ⌃ ⌘ V, and select Values. This keeps your file light and fast. If you need to compare two lists of employees, use the XLOOKUP function. It is faster and more reliable than the old VLOOKUP. It searches columns to the right or left, which is perfect for matching ID numbers against payroll data.

When you are deep in a complex spreadsheet, you do not want to hunt through menus. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur where a specific formatting tool is hiding. Lazur will draw a circle around the button on your screen. If you need to draft a quick email to a manager about a compliance discrepancy, use dictation. Hold fn and speak your message directly into your email app or a note. It keeps your hands on the keyboard and your eyes on your data.

blocks.text: HR compliance hinges on privacy. Always protect your workbooks before sharing them. Go to Review > Protect Sheet to set a password. This stops others from editing your formulas or changing your audit logs. You can also hide gridlines to make your reports look cleaner. Go to View and uncheck Gridlines. It makes your dashboard look professional and ready for an executive presentation.

Keyboard shortcuts save minutes every hour. Use ⌘ T to turn a range into a table. Tables automatically expand when you add new rows, which is great for tracking monthly training completions. Use ⌘ D to fill down the formula from the cell above. Press ⌃ Space to select an entire column for quick formatting. These small movements add up to hours saved over a month.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my Excel files directly?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or edit files for you. It points at tools, guides you through steps, and answers your questions out loud.

faq.question: How do I fix leading zeros disappearing in Excel?
faq.answer: Select the cells, then go to Format > Cells > Number > Text. This forces Excel to treat the numbers as text and keep the leading zeros.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on all Mac versions?
faq.answer: Lazur supports macOS on both Apple silicon and Intel processors. Ensure you are on a recent version of macOS to get the best experience.
